validated_results.title: Dietary boron intake and prostate cancer risk.
validated_results.reason: Original human analysis of dietary boron intake and prostate cancer risk with a quantitative odds ratio.

extraction.comparison_type: highest quartile of dietary boron intake versus lowest quartile
extraction.population: Male participants of the third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES III)

sample_size.excerpt: Cross-sectional case-control study design was employed by comparing boron intake of 95 prostate cancer cases with that of 8,720 male controls.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 95 + 8720 = 8815

cases.excerpt: Cross-sectional case-control study design was employed by comparing boron intake of 95 prostate cancer cases with that of 8,720 male controls.

effect_size.excerpt: The adjusted odds ratio was 0.46 (95% confidence interval: 0.21-0.98) for the highest quartile of boron intake comparing to the lowest quartile (P for trend = 0.0525). The observed association should be interpreted with caution because of the small case sample size and the nature of the cross-sectional study design, but deserve further investigation.

validated_results.title: A case-control study of diet and prostate cancer in Japan: possible protective effect of traditional Japanese diet.
validated_results.reason: Case-control study reporting natto (fermented soybeans) intake and prostate cancer risk with an odds ratio.

extraction.comparison_type: fourth versus first quartile of natto (fermented soybeans) consumption
extraction.population: Prostate cancer cases and age-matched hospital controls in Japan

sample_size.excerpt: We studied 140 cases and 140 individually age ( +/- 5 years)-matched hospital controls for analysis.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 140 + 140 = 280

cases.excerpt: We studied 140 cases and 140 individually age ( +/- 5 years)-matched hospital controls for analysis.

effect_size.excerpt: first quartile and 95% confidence intervals (95%CIs) were 0.45 (0.20-1.02) for fish, 0.53 (0.24-1.14) for all soybean products, 0.47 (0.20-1.08) for tofu, and 0.25 (0.05-1.24) for natto. Consumption of fish and natto showed significantly decreasing linear trends for risk (P < 0.05).

confidence_interval.excerpt: first quartile and 95% confidence intervals (95%CIs) were 0.45 (0.20-1.02) for fish, 0.53 (0.24-1.14) for all soybean products, 0.47 (0.20-1.08) for tofu, and 0.25 (0.05-1.24) for natto.

p_value.excerpt: Consumption of fish and natto showed significantly decreasing linear trends for risk (P < 0.05).
